title: Single-coordinate flip is an involution
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$, a coordinate $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and an $n$-bit Boolean input $x \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$. Writing $\mathrm{flip}_i$ for the operation that negates the $i$-th coordinate of an input and leaves all other coordinates unchanged, applying it twice recovers the original input:
\[
\mathrm{flip}_i\bigl(\mathrm{flip}_i(x)\bigr) = x.
\]
replaced:
For $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and $x : \texttt{BoolInput}(n)$,
$\texttt{flipAt}\,i\,(\texttt{flipAt}\,i\,x) = x$.
That is, applying $\texttt{flipAt}\,i$ twice recovers the original input.
